interpretation: The same Ubuntu endpoints were retained from the 10G test, with only router port/VLAN5 path and 1G bottleneck changed. One VM still supplies both separated network stacks.
5-to-83 paced850 run: 849.987 Mb/s received with 537 retransmissions in30s. Uncapped5-to-83:936.771 Mb/s with2644 retransmissions in60s. 83-to-5:941.421 Mb/s withzero retransmissions in60s.

Both physical interfaces retain zero CRC/input/output errors and output drops in all bracket samples; reset/carrier/pause counters do not increase. Global TailDrop2020 does not increase during any test.

BadUidbSubIdx increases333 to710 across the test brackets and UnconfiguredIpv6Fia406 to409; therefore not every router drop counter is zero. Deleted VLAN5 still allowed by the switch is a plausible background-frame source, not packet-captured proof or attribution to the tested TCP flows.

Retransmissions occur without the Mac adapter. This rules out the adapter as a necessary condition for these new retransmissions, but does not certify the adapter or prove that the older and newer losses have the same cause.

The 1G path direction is useful for localization: inspect switch egress toward router port7 and VM/host networking. No switch counters, packet-loss capture or root cause established. Do not claim a router defect or loss-free network.
No extra paced forward test was needed after the uncapped forward test completed with zero retransmissions and zero new interface/output drops. Long stability gates remain unperformed.
next_steps: Identify switch and physical port feeding router port7; collect transmit queue/drop/error/pause counters bracketing a repeat of the same reverse test before changing offloads or buffers.
If switch evidence is inconclusive, compare packet captures at the Ubuntu sender/receiver and an appropriate switch observation point; consider finer sender pacing as a separate controlled variable.
After resolving the short-test scope, execute a defined 60-minute monitored forwarding gate, remaining idle gate, three corrected cold boots and overnight soak; do not count mixed uptime as a gate.
